reporting-org.narrative: The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria

title.narrative: Improving quality and access to TB services by supporting early case detection; integrated patient centered care and prevention; addressing the threats DR-TB - Mongolia (01-Jan-2018-31-Dec-2020)

description.narrative: Mongolia, Tuberculosis, Ministry of Health of Mongolia (MOH Mongolia)This program has the following goals: To improve treatment success rate up to 90% and decrease TB related mortality by 30% compared to 2015 by the end of 2020.. The objectives of this program are: To improve TB case notification from 37% (2015) to 49% by 2020.. To increase treatment success rate of RR TB and/or MDR TB from 67% (2016) to 73% by 2020.. To enroll all HIV-positive new and relapse TB patients in ART during TB treatment.

title.narrative: Coverage / Output indicators targets and results for MNG-T-MOHP04
Percentage of HIV-positive new and relapse TB patients on ART during TB treatment
Number of cases with RR-TB and/or MDR-TB that began second-line treatment
Number of TB cases with RR-TB and/or MDR-TB notified
Number of notified cases of all forms of TB (i.e. bacteriologically confirmed + clinically diagnosed), new and relapse cases

Treatment success rate- all forms: Percentage of TB cases, all forms, bacteriologically confirmed plus clinically diagnosed, successfully treated (cured plus treatment completed) among all TB cases registered for treatment during a specified period, new and relapse cases
Outcome indicators targets and results for MNG-T-MOHP04

TB treatment coverage: Percentage of patients with new and relapse TB that were notified and treated among the estimated number of incident TB in the same year (all forms of TB - bacteriologically confirmed plus clinically diagnosed
Treatment success rate of RR-TB and/or MDR-TB: Percentage of patients with RR and/or MDR-TB successfully treated
Impact indicators targets and results for MNG-T-MOHP04
TB I-Other 1: Proportion of RR-TB and/or MDR-TB prevalence among smear positive and retreatment TB cases
